content.text:
All 9 tests pass, 2 remain as todo.

🟢 Green Phase Complete:
**Implementation**: Added a de-duplication clause to the existing `bornCells` filter in `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-07-25_23-41-37_game-of-life-example-mapping_v4-exact-subagents_opus-5-no-thinking/src/game-of-life.ts` — a candidate is kept only when its index is the first index at which that coordinate appears:

```ts
candidates.findIndex((other) => isSameCell(candidate, other)) === index
```

**Result**: All tests now pass (9 passing, 2 todo)

**Approach**: This is minimal because it changes nothing about the birth rule itself and adds no new helper, data structure, or abstraction. The test demanded exactly one new property — set semantics on the result — and the smallest way to get it was one extra predicate in the filter that was already there, reusing the existing `isSameCell`. A `Set`-based keying scheme or a dedicated `unique` helper would have been more machinery than the current test forces; the O(n²) `findIndex` is fine at these sizes and any performance concern belongs to Refactor, not here. Note the duplicates only ever arose in `bornCells` (survivors come from the already-unique input), so no change was needed on the survivor branch.

Proceeding to Refactor phase.
